severity_name: SEVERE SLOP WARNING — COORDINATED INAUTHENTICITY ADVISORY
headline: SEVERE SLOP WARNING: SOCKPUPPET-CHORUS FRONT SETTLES OVER FIVE REGIONS AS INDUSTRIAL VOLUMES OF CHEAP SYNTHETIC OPINION ARRIVE FROM THOUSANDS OF ACCOUNTS THAT SHARE ONE HEARTBEAT AND NO ACTUAL PERSON
advisory: A large, slow-moving influence system has stalled over the eastern feed corridors, producing sustained downpours of mass-manufactured commentary engineered to resemble spontaneous public agreement. The Service notes that the individual particles are low-effort by design; the hazard is volume, not quality, and the system's purpose is to make a manufactured mood feel like weather. Residents are advised that ten thousand accounts posting the identical sentiment do not constitute ten thousand people. Consensus, this week, is not a reading you can trust off the surface.

regional_outlook.conditions: Dense sockpuppet fog reduces visibility to near zero, with identical replies pooling under unrelated posts. A manufactured trend is expected to crest by midafternoon and evaporate the moment it is examined.
Coordinated reshare currents push the same three talking points through hundreds of tributary groups. Elderly residents are advised the neighborhood mood is being simulated upstream.
Scattered astroturf blooms disguised as grassroots enthusiasm for a product no plateau resident has used. Engagement remains high; sincerity remains at record lows.
Runoff from the chorus is seeping into the citation layer, where synthetic opinion is being mistaken for public sentiment. Expect murky, recirculated water through the evening.
Tidal influx of 'concerned constituent' form messages, each unique in phrasing and identical in origin. Filter integrity holding, but strained.

specimen.status: Abundant and coordinated; population figures unreliable, as it is one puppeteer wearing many gloves
specimen.habitat: Reply threads, quote-posts, comment sections, and any venue where a number of voices is mistaken for a weight of opinion
specimen.field_marks: Dozens to thousands of accounts arriving in tight formation, each with a stock-photo face and a handle ending in eight random digits, all landing the same phrase within the same nine-minute window. Bios are plausible; posting histories begin, suspiciously, last Tuesday.
specimen.call: As an ordinary person who thought about this independently, I have to say I completely agree with everyone else here.
specimen.confusion_species: Easily mistaken for genuine public consensus. Distinguish by cadence: a real crowd disagrees, wanders off-topic, and misspells things with personality, while the Chorus arrives on schedule, stays perfectly on message, and never once changes its mind or asks what you meant.

spotter_tip: When a hundred strangers phrase their heartfelt personal opinion in the exact same word order, you are not witnessing agreement — you are witnessing a copy-paste with a wardrobe budget. Check the account birthdays; a movement born last Tuesday is a costume, not a crowd.
tomorrow: Chorus front weakens to scattered bot-drizzle, but a fresh coordination cell is organizing offshore and may make landfall by Thursday afternoon.

confirmed_sighting.report: Researchers report that some of the largest online propaganda and influence campaigns are increasingly relying on cheap, mass-produced AI-generated content — 'slop' — to flood social platforms. The Service notes the strategy prizes quantity over craft, which is precisely the pattern our instruments are built to detect.
